Why we’re supporting a common signal that lets website operators communicate their choices to multiple AI providers at once.

Today, we’re announcing that OpenAI will honor a commonsignal⁠(opens in a new window)in robots.txt, the file that lets websites express their preferences about the use of their content for foundational generative AI training. This voluntary effort makes it easier for publishers and website operators to communicate the same preference to multiple participating providers at once.

Previously, website operators would identify individual crawlers and maintain separate rules for each and every provider. Having a shared signal across multiple providers reduces that work for operators.

We aim to implement the signal in the coming months, and will share another update with details about our implementation when we do so. This new signal will not replace the controls we already provide through robots.txt. Our existingcrawler controls⁠(opens in a new window), which provide web publishers flexibility and control over their pages, will continue to apply and be respected.

This draws on theongoing work⁠(opens in a new window)of the Internet Engineering Task Force’s (IETF) AI Preferences working group. We’re joining other participants in the working group in today’s announcement of this shared signal, and believe this strengthens our continued participation in the IETF standards discussions. OpenAI will continue to adapt its practices as those conversations and the landscape continue to evolve in view of appropriate controls and fairness.

We believe this is a practical step toward an open web where people can publish and discover information, and website owners have clearer, simpler ways to communicate their choices about how their content is used. We encourage other AI providers to honor the signal.

articles.title: Safety
articles.content:
October 30, 2026

ChatGPT is one of the world’s most widely used AI products, and we have invested in building some of the industry’s most advanced systems for detecting potential harm, reviewing concerning activity, and escalating credible threats. We’re making two announcements to further our work in this area: a new Community Safeguards Report and more restrictions around firearms content for minors.

Keeping communities safe⁠continues to be a top priority for OpenAI. Our work includes bringing imminent threats of violence to the attention of law enforcement, andwe made over 200 law enforcement referrals in Q3 2026.These referrals are making apositive⁠(opens in a new window)difference⁠(opens in a new window)in disrupting violent plots, and we continue to rely on mental health and behavioral experts to help us assess difficult cases.

We recognize AI companies have a distinct role to play alongside law enforcement, family members, mental-health professionals, and policymakers, who bring critical authority, context and real-world reach. We are committed to making the most of that role by continuously strengthening our systems, sharing what we learn, and working directly with those who are best positioned to act in the real world.

We are constantly strengthening the steps we take to help protect people and communities. That means building strong safeguards, and also being transparent about how well they work and what we’re doing to enhance them. We want to give people a clear picture of our approach, how our models identify and respond to harmful behavior, the risks we see in practice, and the steps we take to address them.

We’re committing to launch the Community Safety Report on violence prevention and other community safety issues, and the effectiveness of our safeguards. The report will explain how we train our systems to detect, investigate, and respond to community safety issues. We’ll share anonymized examples of how violence-related harm manifests and what we’re learning, highlight new mitigations and policy changes, and include relevant data to support these findings.

We will publish our first report in early 2027, covering the second half of 2026, with updates every six months thereafter. Our commitment is to share meaningful findings about how we identify, review, and respond to potentially harmful content.

Our models are trained to not give instructions that would help someone plan or carry out violence. We’re now placing additional restrictions on how ChatGPT responds to questions about past mass attacks and the people who carried them out, directing the model to provide less detailed information in those areas even if it is available from other online sources. People should be able to ask ChatGPT to help them understand these events, how victims and communities were impacted, and learn about recognizing warning signs and preventing future violence. But we’re tightening our policies to restrict reconstructions of past mass attacks, including details about the weapons and equipment used and how they were obtained, and detailed comparisons on scale of harm that could amplify an attacker’s notoriety. These limits apply regardless of a user’s age or reason for asking.

Sometimes a request that seems ordinary on its own takes on a different meaning in light of an earlier conversation. In May, we shared howChatGPT can use short, factual summaries⁠of earlier warning signs to respond more carefully in a later chat. We’re building on that work so that when recent chats show warning signs of possible violence, ChatGPT will respond more conservatively when sharing information that could be misused. We’re also working to apply those stricter limits when we predict someone is under 18, even if their chats show no signs of violent intent.

We ban accounts that we determine have violated ourpolicies on violent activity⁠. We’re also working with mental health and violence prevention experts on additional, automated ways to intervene earlier. When a conversation shows signs that someone is fixating on violence or the idea of seriously harming another person, ChatGPT will be able to automatically end the chat to interrupt that pattern in the moment. If ChatGPT ends multiple chats for that reason, we may temporarily pause the account. This is an ongoing effort and we continue to strengthen and invest in technical and practical protections, including how to recognize warning signs reliably and determine when and how to intervene.

ChatGPT for Teens⁠applies age-appropriate safeguards for users under 18, with stronger protections and additional limits to reduce exposure to sensitive content. We’re now placing further limits on weapons-related information teens can receive, even when a question appears harmless.

Our policies already prohibit helping anyone plan or carry out violence and restrict helping teens find or obtain weapons. We’re extending those protections to restrict practical information about weapons and security systems that could be misused to facilitate violence, even when there’s no sign of violent intent. Teens can still use ChatGPT to help prevent and de-escalate violence, seek support, and connect with a trusted adult.

We launchedage prediction⁠last year, which analyzes multiple signals such as behavior patterns to estimate whether a user may be under or over 18. We strengthened our age prediction system to continually assess new signals as people use ChatGPT and move teens into the under 18 experience when appropriate. Users who are incorrectly placed in the under 18 experience will always have a fast, privacy-protective way to confirm they are adults and have additional teen protections removed through Persona, our age verification partner.

Ourparental controls⁠let parents link their ChatGPT accounts to their teens and manage safety settings together. Linked accounts includesafety alerts⁠that may be sent when specially trained reviewers identify a serious self-harm concern and behaviors that may be associated with disordered eating. In July, we expanded those alerts to notify parents if their teen’s account has been deactivated for violating our usage policies on violence. We are working to introduce notifications for parents if we pause their teen’s account for repeatedly discussing violence, as detailed above.

Acts of real-world violence are heartbreaking and complex, with many contributing factors. They are also a stark reminder that we must continue designing and iterating our systems to account for the inherently complicated realities of human behavior. Developing effective violence safeguards in AI systems requires solving novel problems in recognizing risk and responding appropriately, and we will continue to invest in, iterate, and share learnings  on how best to implement the protections we’re pursuing. The safeguards detailed here will begin rolling out in the next few weeks and we will continue to refine them. We remain committed to mitigating risks of harm in ChatGPT, strengthening our layered protections, monitoring for misuse, enforcing our rules, and involving real-world support and interventions when situations call for it.

articles.title: Samaya AI Releases Sterling: A 3B-Active Finance Research Agent Model that Beats Claude Fable 5.1 on FrontierFinance at 11x Lower Cost
articles.content: Samaya AI has released Samaya Sterling, a post-trained model for agentic financial research. Sterling is built on NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 3B active parameters. On Samaya’s FrontierFinance benchmark, it scores 58.9%. Claude Fable 5.1 scores 55.9%. Each Sterling question costs $0.61, against $6.89 for Fable 5.1. For developers, the takeaway is a concrete recipe: co-train a small model with its harness, and it can win in a narrow domain. TL;DR Size: 30B total, 3B active (MoE). Base model context: up to 1M tokens. Sterling’s serving context: not disclosed. Runs on: the base model fits a single H100 80GB in BF16 (256K context). Sterling’s serving hardware: not disclosed. Performance: beats every high-quality system on the FrontierFinance leaderboard on quality per dollar (self-reported). Best: 58.9% on FrontierFinance (60.6% in high-effort mode), vs 55.9% for Claude Fable 5.1. Worst: 45.2% on the hardest third of FrontierFinance questions. What is Samaya Sterling? Samaya Sterling is a LoRA post-trained version of Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, tuned to work as a financial research agent. It plans research, calls finance tools, gathers evidence and hands findings to a separate report writer. According to Maithra Raghu’s X announcement, it started as a 2-person effort on agentic orchestration efficiency. How does the harness support a 3B-active model? Samaya team adapted its production finance harness for a small model. Detailed guidance was stripped from the system prompt and tool descriptions. Tools were merged to shorten the prompt. Two helper models manage context. A condenser shortens long tool results. A compactor summarizes the trace as it grows. A research budget caps how long the agent works. After that, the report writer answers from what was found. How was Sterling trained? Training used LoRA on Tinker, Thinking Machines Lab’s training API. It ran in 4 stages: SFT on synthetic traces: Samaya generated 968 synthetic analyst questions. The teacher, Kimi K3, answered each twice, and an LLM judge picked the better answer. The model learned to call 37 tools with valid arguments. SFT on the best of 8 strategies: Kimi K3 answered 1,819 expert-written questions using 8 research strategies. The best-graded answer per question became training data. Best-of-8 met 80% of essential rubric items, against about 66% for the single best strategy. After filtering, 1,157 questions remained. Offline GRPO: GRPO scored all 8 teacher answers against each other. No new generation was needed, so each step was cheap. Online GRPO: The model answered each question 8 times and learned from graded attempts. Truncated importance sampling corrected a known MoE sampler mismatch. How does Sterling score on FrontierFinance? FrontierFinance has 220 public queries scored against expert-written rubrics. The grader uses a 3-model judge panel. Samaya team states that no benchmark question was used in training. Checkpoints were chosen on 100 internal validation questions. Sterling scores 58.9% at $0.61 and 282 s per question. Fable 5.1 scores 55.9% at $6.89 and 268 s. Samaya’s own high-effort system scores 2.9 points lower at $1.81. Every stage added quality: 42.5% (base), 51.4%, 54.8%, 57.5%, then 58.9%. Median tool calls rose from 3 to 17. In high-effort mode, Sterling reaches 60.6% at $1.83 and 372 s. On the hardest third, it rose from 31.8% to 45.2%. The model itself costs $0.04 per question. Tools and helper models make up the rest of the $0.61. && How does Sterling compare? articles.title: Meet TokenEconomizer: Microsoft’s Plugin That Cuts Coding Agent Costs by Up to 30.9%
articles.content: A team of researchers from Microsoft Research and UC Berkeley have released TokenEconomizer, an open-source cost controller for coding agents. TokenEconomizer is a plugin that learns from past sessions in a repository to cut waste in later ones. It works with Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI and Pi. It does not touch model weights or agent code. On 277 SWE-Bench tasks, it lowered mean cost by 18.4% to 30.9% across 5 agent-model settings. TL;DR Package: A standard-library Python package and agent plugins, with 3 switchable mechanisms. Runs on: Any machine running Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI or Pi with Python 3.10+. No GPU and no API key of its own. Performance: 18.4% to 30.9% lower mean SWE-Bench cost, and cheaper in all 30 repository-setting cells. Best: 30.9% lower cost on Claude Code with Opus 4.8 (33.2% when combined with RTK). Worst: Only 6.4% to 9.3% savings on ReposVul audits; Pass@1 drops 1.0 point on Opus 4.8. Why do coding agents waste tokens? Every agent turn re-bills the system prompt, every loaded tool schema and the full history. The research team profiled 60 SWE-Bench tasks across 6 repositories using Claude Code with Opus 4.8. They found 3 recurring sources of waste: Repeated discovery: once 5 tasks precede the current one, 30% of tool calls repeat an earlier action. Unused tools: 23 tool schemas load every turn. 16 are never called, and 3 cover 98% of calls. Failure loops: 10 failed runs were 17% of tasks but 32% of total spend. They also tested 3 fixed open-source strategies: RTK, Serena and Aider’s RepoMap. None was cheaper everywhere. All 3 cut cost on Django and raised it on SymPy. How does TokenEconomizer work? TokenEconomizer is an external controller that treats the agent as a black box. It keeps a state per repository, built from completed traces. Before each task, it sets 3 policies through the prompt, the tool settings and the event stream. 1. Micro-skills An LLM proposer turns trace digests into 1-line facts, such as the working test command. Each fact carries regex detectors that check later traces without a model call. A fact enters the prompt after 3 confirmations on tasks with non-overlapping edited files. Its need rate must also stay at or above 0.4. One contradiction counts as 5 confirmations, so wrong facts retire quickly. 2. Tool pruning Shell, read, write and edit tools are always kept. Other tools are masked after 3 consecutive unused tasks, or when an LLM judge marks them irrelevant. The full catalog returns every 5 tasks for a re-audit. On Django with Claude Code, the first request on task 2 fell from 43,351 to 16,295 prompt tokens. 3. Failure-loop intervention The controller learns a turn budget: 1.25 times the 90th percentile of successful run lengths. Cheap rule checks flag repeated failures or dense errors. An LLM judge then decides if the agent is stuck, at 0.7 confidence or higher. A stuck agent gets 1 redirect, then a stop if the loop recurs. && What do the SWE-Bench results show? Costs include all controller calls. 3 seeds per setting. Pass@1 improved in 4 of 5 settings. Lower reasoning effort saved cost but cut Pass@1 by 1.8 to 10.3 points. RTK alone raised cost in 12 of 30 repository-setting cells, and RepoMap in 15. Savings build over time. Most repositories cost more at first, but all were cheaper by the sixth task. Alone on Claude Code, tool pruning saved 13.2% to 17.7%, micro-skills 11.8% to 14.3%, and the loop guard 5.4% to 7.1%. Results also held outside SWE-Bench. Costs fell 16.0% to 21.2% on Web-Bench and 16.5% to 19.6% on CredData. ReposVul saw only 6.4% to 9.3%, because shorter runs leave less to remove. How does it compare with other token-saving tools? On Claude Code, clone the repo, add it as a marketplace, then run claude plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer. Learned data stays local in ~/.tokeneconomizer. Tool pruning and the loop guard are on by default. Micro-skills are off by default, because the proposer adds model calls. articles.title: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence
articles.content: At a glance Evaluating Microsoft Copilot at enterprise scale requires test data that captures the full complexity of real organizations, yet real enterprise data contains sensitive information that cannot be used for evaluation under any circumstances. To resolve this tension, we built Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform: full-scale synthetic enterprise environments grounded in publicly available real-world data sources such as O*NET occupational data, online job postings, and SEC filings. The synthetic environments mimic real business workflows, helping Microsoft find issues that generic benchmarks would miss. Safety and privacy are built into the platform by design. Every environment is fully synthetic and automated content-safety checks keep the generated data free of harmful or personally identifiable material. Every day, millions of knowledge workers around the world rely on Microsoft Copilot to draft documents, summarize meetings, surface relevant information, and accelerate productivity. Behind the scenes, this is powered by a network of AI systems, and ensuring they work as intended requires a thoughtful approach to evaluation. At Microsoft, we know that high performance doesn’t come from guesswork. It comes from testing, measuring, and iterating constantly. Healthcare organizations are constantly synthesizing safety signals from across teams so that they can make faster, better decisions that directly influence patient outcomes and regulatory confidence. They may ask Copilot to summarize a meeting and extract action items for their teams. Within seconds, Copilot delivers a structured summary citing specific discussion points from the transcript. But how do we ensure this response is accurate, complete, and properly grounded in the meeting content? This is where our evaluation system comes in. We’ve developed a structured evaluation strategy called Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform, which includes industry specific evaluation datasets designed to test AI systems against realistic enterprise scenarios, grounded in three core pillars: Synthetic enterprise environments: simulated Microsoft Copilot environments with realistic users, meetings, emails, documents, and organizational structures that replicate the complexity of real organizations without using any customer data Automated query generation pipelines for rapid, reproducible creation of evaluation datasets Structured quality frameworks to ensure synthetic data meets the bar for meaningful evaluation Figure 1: Components of Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform Together, these pillars help us answer two fundamental questions: Is Microsoft Copilot actually doing what our users need it to do, and can we prove it without ever touching their data? In this blog post, we’ll walk through our evaluation system and processes, from synthetic environment generation to automated query pipelines, and how it all comes together to establish the first standardized evaluation baseline for Microsoft Copilot. Synthetic enterprise environments Evaluating enterprise AI requires test data that captures the full complexity of real organizations: reporting structures, project histories, communication patterns, and domain specific workflows. But real enterprise data contains sensitive information that cannot be used for evaluation under any circumstances. This is the central tension we set out to resolve. Rather than relying on small, manually curated test fixtures, we generate full scale synthetic environments: simulated enterprise workspaces, each with realistic organizational structures, communication histories, and work artifacts. In Microsoft terminology, each of these simulated workspaces is called a “tenant”. A tenant is an isolated organizational environment with its own users, data, and configurations. These environments are scalable baselines that teams and organizations can build off of however they want. They are designed to exhibit the same structural and behavioral properties that make enterprise AI evaluation meaningful. Grounding in real world signals To ensure our synthetic environments are realistic, we grounded them in publicly available real world data sources. O*NET data from the U.S. Department of Labor’s occupational database was used to make synthetic employee roles and responsibilities realistic, calibrate the mix and frequency of work activities assigned to different roles, and tailor industry specific workflows such as clinical trial reviews or portfolio updates. Online job postings provide realistic role titles, reporting hierarchies, and departmental compositions. SEC filings inform organizational scale, business unit structures, and financial contexts. All of these sources are publicly available and have been reviewed and approved by Microsoft’s legal and policy organization. Figure 2: Real signals from public datasets that are used to ground the evaluation data generation Importantly, these synthetic environments are not static snapshots. They simulate dynamic, time-evolving organizations with meeting histories, project timelines, email threads that develop over weeks, and organizational changes that unfold naturally. This temporal dimension is essential because a large class of Copilot queries are inherently time aware. Questions like “What did the team decide last Thursday?” or “What’s changed since the last quarterly review?” only produce meaningful evaluations if the underlying data has a genuine temporal structure. Industry specific simulation We generated three synthetic environments across multiple industries, each with distinct characteristics that mirror real world usage: A pharmaceutical environment that includes regulatory submission workflows, clinical trial discussions, and cross functional safety review meetings A capital markets environment featuring deal pipelines, compliance communications, and client portfolio reviews An IT/software company that simulates sprint planning, code review discussions, and product launch coordination Figure 3: Industries targeted for industry evaluation data generation This industry specificity ensures that our evaluation queries test Copilot against the kinds of questions real users in those domains actually ask, rather than relying on generic test cases that may not surface domain specific failure modes. Automated query generation While synthetic environments provide the substrate for evaluation, they face a key limitation: we still need realistic evaluation queries. These are the questions that test whether Copilot can surface the right information, synthesize it correctly, and present it helpfully. Manually writing thousands of grounded, industry specific queries is prohibitively expensive and slow. That’s where our automated pipeline comes in. The six-stage pipeline Figure 4: Query customization pipeline that turns generic query templates into realistic, industry-specific queries We built an automated pipeline that turns simple, generic query ideas into realistic, industry-specific questions for Copilot. It starts with a large library of common workplace tasks, narrows them down to what’s relevant for a given industry, and adapts them using domain-specific language and context. The system then uses AI to generate queries grounded in the synthetic environment’s data, rewrites them to sound more natural and human, and validates each one for accuracy and uniqueness. The result is a rich set of high-quality, lifelike queries that enable scalable and reliable evaluation of Copilot across real-world scenarios. Validating synthetic quality Of course, generating synthetic data is only part of the challenge. We also need to ensure the data is good enough to produce meaningful evaluations. We assess synthetic environment quality using our internal semantic evaluation framework which measures quality across three dimensions: Structural fidelity: Does the organizational structure reflect realistic reporting hierarchies, team sizes, and cross functional relationships? Contextual relevance: Are the queries and workflows representative of actual enterprise usage patterns? Behavioral realism: Do the simulated users exhibit human-like communication patterns and collaboration dynamics? Content safety: Is the generated content free of harmful, offensive, or personally identifiable material, and does it avoid impersonating real individuals? End-to-end automation While our synthetic environments and query pipelines provide the methodology, they face several practical limitations without proper automation, including: Reproducibility: Manual processes produce subtly different results each time, making it difficult to compare evaluations across releases. Scale: The number of industry verticals and configuration variants exceeds what any team can reasonably produce by hand. Iteration speed: Manual creation takes days, delaying essential feedback and slowing down development cycles. Cross-team consistency: Without standardized tooling, different teams produce evaluation datasets with incompatible formats and quality levels. This automation reduced evaluation dataset creation from a multi-day manual process to automated runs. We estimate savings of approximately $100,000 per evaluation dataset and $300,000 in total project savings. But the more important outcome is that any team can now regenerate an evaluation dataset from the same configuration and get identical results. ACADEMIC CONFERENCE Microsoft at SOSP 2026 Academic and industrial participants present research and experience papers that cover the full range of theory and practice of computer systems software. Learn more Opens in a new tab Privacy and safety by design Enterprise grade evaluation demands more than good methodology. It requires a privacy posture that allows teams to move fast without compromising user trust. A non-negotiable design principle of our industry evaluation datasets is that no real customer data is used at any
articles.summary: Microsoft는 민감한 실제 기업 데이터를 쓰지 않고 Copilot을 평가하기 위한 Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform을 소개했다. O*NET 직업 정보, 채용 공고, SEC 공시 등 공개 자료를 바탕으로 조직의 업무 흐름을 모사하는 대규모 합성 기업 환경을 생성한다. 범용 벤치마크가 놓치는 산업별 문제를 찾는 것이 목적이며, 자동 콘텐츠 안전 점검으로 유해하거나 개인을 식별할 수 있는 자료를 배제하도록 설계했다. 제공된 설명에는 정량적인 평가 개선치가 없어, 실제 조직 환경을 얼마나 충실히 재현하는지는 추가 검증이 필요하다.

articles.title: Edge0 Releases Audio8-TTS-Realistic, a 0.6B Voice Cloning TTS Model
articles.content: Edge0 has released Audio8-TTS-Realistic, an open-weight text-to-speech model for zero-shot voice cloning. Audio8-TTS-Realistic is a 0.6B-parameter model that clones a voice from 1 reference clip and transcript. It supports 23 languages, 12 more than its predecessor. The weights and code ship under Apache 2.0. For developers, the catch is competitive multilingual accuracy at a size that is cheap to fine-tune and serve. TL;DR Size: 601M main-model parameters (codec excluded); up to 2,048 packed text/audio positions of context. Runs on: a CUDA GPU is recommended; smoke-tested on NVIDIA H20 in BF16. The paper reports 1.1 to 1.2 GiB peak memory on an Apple M2 CPU (INT4 ONNX). No Realistic ONNX export is public yet. Performance: ahead of larger open models on CV3, behind 4B-class models on MiniMax. Best: 4.86% average CV3 error across 9 languages, versus 7.73% for Qwen3-TTS-1.7B. Worst: 48.57% WER on Thai (CV3) and 31.35% CER on Cantonese (MiniMax). What is Audio8-TTS-Realistic? It is the second 0.6B release in Edge0’s Audio8 TTS family. It builds on Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b and keeps the same Transformers inference interface. The repository bundles the checkpoint, a 44.1 kHz neural audio codec, tokenizer, processor and custom code. It can also generate speech without a reference voice. New languages are Arabic, Finnish, Hindi, Indonesian, Malay, Norwegian, Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese. How does the architecture work? The model uses a dual-autoregressive (DualAR) design inspired by Fish Audio S2 Pro. According to the technical research report, the slow branch is built on Qwen2.5 0.5B. It has 24 layers at width 896 and runs at about 21.5 frames per second. Each step predicts text tokens plus the first audio codebook. A shallow 4-layer fast branch then predicts the remaining 9 codebooks in parallel. Sequential compute therefore happens only at the frame level. How does Edge0 train for realism? The team argues that word error rate (WER) and speaker similarity (SIM) miss rhythm, pauses and timing. A model can score well on both and still sound synthetic. Training runs in 3 stages: Multilingual supervised fine-tuning (SFT). GRPO with a combined reward: 0.7 weight on WER, 0.3 on SIM. GRPO guided by a learned realism critic. The critic scores each output against a matched human recording of the same sentence. It was trained on a quality ladder built from 6 open-source TTS systems. These were ranked in a private blind listening study, with human recordings at the top. Synthetic pause compression adds finer rungs to the ladder. An identity-erasure loss stops the critic from rewarding generator fingerprints. The critic head has about 3M parameters on top of a frozen WavLM-large encoder. A duration penalty also kicks in beyond 1.35x the reference length. This blocks the policy from gaming the critic with slower speech. The final stage used only Chinese and English prompts. It still improved both aggregate metrics on the 13 lower-resource languages. Their error fell from 22.53% to 20.77%, and SIM rose from 0.637 to 0.679. articles.title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.37786v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Web agents require diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for reproducible training and evaluation. Human-assisted mirrors demand per-site engineering, while generative construction can diverge from specified real websites. Capture-and-replay preserves observations, with interaction coverage constrained by captured content and replay capabilities.
  We present WebAnything, a fully automated framework that reconstructs source-grounded, reusable Web environments from real URLs without per-site manual implementation or repair after initial setup and authorization. An Explorer-Builder collects browser-observable structures, resources, and interaction outcomes; an independent verifier checks frozen candidates and guides local repair or targeted source recapture.
  We construct 244 website artifacts across 14 application domains and 53 categories, supporting 12,984 executed and accepted tasks. Compared with human-assisted WebHarbor, WebAnything achieves higher aggregate scores on three fidelity metrics, with 12 wins, two ties, and no losses in a blind audit. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B on 5,856 interaction trajectories improves REAL success by 9.9 percentage points, Odysseys-Easy Rubric Avg and Task Avg by 6.25 and 6.32 percentage points, and WebArena-Verified Overall success by 13.33 percentage points under the fixed harness. Code: https://github.com/china-qijizhifeng/Web-Anything
articles.summary: WebAnything은 실제 URL에서 브라우저로 관찰할 수 있는 구조·자원·상호작용을 수집해 재사용 가능한 웹 에이전트 학습 환경을 자동 재구성한다. 초기 설정과 권한 부여 이후 사이트별 수동 구현 없이 탐색·구축 모듈과 독립 검증기가 환경을 만들고 수정하도록 설계했다. 연구진은 14개 응용 분야의 웹사이트 환경 244개와 실행·승인된 과제 12,984개를 구축했으며, 수집 궤적으로 Qwen3.5-9B를 미세조정했을 때 고정 평가 조건에서 WebArena-Verified 성공률이 13.33%포인트 높아졌다고 보고했다. 웹 자동화 연구의 환경 제작 부담을 줄일 가능성이 있으며 코드도 공개했다.

articles.title: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.37720v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models offer scalable capacity for Web applications, but uneven routing creates computation and communication bottlenecks. Existing placement and replication methods redistribute this workload, yet additional expert copies compete with token-related buffers for limited GPU memory. We present LRMoE, a memory-aware MoE training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances the retained workload. During forward execution, it plans retention quotas and expert placement under resource constraints while preserving all routed computations. During backpropagation, a load recalibration metric estimates each token-expert pair's contribution to the expert update and selects pairs within these quotas. A capacity-aware routing algorithm distributes retained pairs among eligible instances of their original experts. Physical compaction then forms smaller communication payloads and variable-size grouped GEMMs, reducing backward traffic, computation, and execution-buffer demand. Experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B show that LRMoE reduces cumulative MoE-layer training time to fixed-loss targets by 21.2-44.8% relative to SYMI.
articles.summary: LRMoE는 GPU 메모리가 제한된 환경에서 전문가 혼합 모델의 역전파 작업량과 전문가 배치를 함께 조절하는 학습 시스템이다. 순전파의 라우팅 연산은 모두 유지하되, 역전파에서는 전문가 갱신 기여도를 추정해 토큰·전문가 쌍을 선택하고 이를 압축해 통신량과 연산·버퍼 수요를 줄인다. Qwen3-30B-A3B와 GLM4.5-106B-A12B 실험에서 목표 손실까지의 누적 MoE 계층 학습 시간이 SYMI 대비 21.2~44.8% 감소했다. 전체 학습 시간의 동일한 감소를 입증한 수치는 아니지만, 메모리와 부하 불균형이 동시에 병목인 MoE 학습에 유용한 접근이다.

articles.title: world2vec: Mechanistic world models through latent dynamics learning
articles.content: World models can achieve strong control performance without faithfully capturing the dynamics of their environment, limiting their potential for mechanistic interpretability and scientific discovery. Here, we introduce world2vec to learn mechanistic world models without reward information directly from observations and actions. World2vec learns latent dynamics that faithfully reproduce the true system over long prediction horizons, with at least one order of magnitude fewer parameters than DreamerV3, TD-MPC2 and LeWM. This enables state of the art performance in controlling continuous environments from pixels and accurate system identification across a benchmark of 71 attractors, demonstrating how world models are amenable to scientific discovery.
articles.summary: world2vec는 보상 정보 없이 관측과 행동에서 잠재 동역학을 학습해 환경의 실제 움직임을 장기간 재현하려는 월드 모델이다. 연구진은 DreamerV3, TD-MPC2, LeWM보다 최소 한 자릿수 규모, 즉 약 10배 이상 적은 파라미터로 픽셀 기반 연속 환경 제어에서 최상위 성능을 달성했다고 보고했다. 또한 71개 어트랙터 벤치마크에서 정확한 시스템 식별을 제시하며, 제어 성능뿐 아니라 물리적 메커니즘 이해를 목표로 삼았다. 과학적 발견과 효율적인 제어 모델 개발에 의미가 있지만, 제공된 초록에는 상세 성능 수치나 적용 범위의 한계가 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: LucidLyra: Feed-Forward Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction and Joint Understanding via Multi-Task Distillation
articles.content: We present LucidLyra, a framework that makes generatively reconstructed 3D scenes directly queryable for semantics and instances in a feed-forward manner from video latents. While generative 3D reconstruction can synthesize virtual environments from a single image, downstream applications in robotics and physical AI require not only visual realism but also access to scene semantics and object identities. Existing 3D understanding approaches, however, require captured multi-view scenes, have limited generalization capabilities, or rely on expensive per-scene processing and optimization. To bridge this gap, our method distills complementary knowledge from a camera-controlled video diffusion model and frozen 2D vision foundation models into a unified model to jointly infer 3D Gaussians encoding geometry, appearance, open-vocabulary semantics, and class-agnostic instance cues. The resulting scenes support novel-view rendering, open-vocabulary segmentation, and object grouping without per-scene optimization, while training requires neither manual 3D annotations nor captured multi-view data. Our method outperforms baselines combining state-of-the-art 3DGS segmentation approaches with generative 3D scene reconstruction on curated synthetic and real-image-conditioned benchmarks, while preserving reconstruction quality. Furthermore, our latent formulation naturally extends to monocular video, reconstructing structured dynamic 3D scenes across time. By turning renderable but unstructured outputs into queryable 3D worlds, LucidLyra enables downstream applications including 3D scene editing, 3D asset mining, and robotic simulation.
articles.summary: LucidLyra는 카메라 제어형 비디오 확산 모델과 동결된 2D 비전 기반 모델의 지식을 증류해, 형상·외관·의미·객체 단서를 함께 갖춘 3D 가우시안 장면을 생성한다. 장면별 최적화 없이 새로운 시점 렌더링, 개방형 어휘 분할, 객체 그룹화를 지원하며 수동 3D 주석이나 촬영된 다중 시점 데이터 없이 학습한다. 연구진은 합성 및 실제 이미지 조건부 벤치마크에서 재구성 품질을 유지하면서 비교 방법보다 우수한 장면 이해 성능을 보고했고, 단안 비디오의 동적 장면으로도 확장했다. 단순히 보는 3D 결과물을 검색·편집 가능한 구조로 바꿔 로봇 시뮬레이션과 3D 자산 활용에 연결하는 접근이다.

articles.title: AI Security Agents Compared: Claude, Codex, Mantis, Cloudflare
articles.content: Anthropic, OpenAI, Cloudflare and Google now each ship an AI agent that hunts security bugs in source code. We checked the repos, docs and technical details behind each one. The key finding: all 4 tools converge on one design. One agent finds a bug, a separate agent tries to disprove it, and only survivors get a patch. The differences are in where they run, who can use them and how much proof they demand. Key Takeaways 4 labs, 1 pattern: find, independently disprove, then patch. Claude Security runs inside Claude Code; no extra API key needed. Codex Security’s CLI is Apache-2.0, but scanning still needs OpenAI access. Cloudflare’s skill is MIT, model-agnostic and the most-starred at 47.5K. Google’s Mantis reproduces bugs in a sandbox; Google says isolate it. Why 4 labs shipped the same thing in 2026 The problem every one of them is solving is noise. Google’s security team writes that sloppy AI code scanning produces hallucinated bugs and true-positive rates under 7%. A scanner that is wrong 93% of the time costs reviewers more than it saves. The shared fix is separation of duties. The agent that reports a finding never gets to confirm it. Cloudflare states the rule directly in its README: the verifier is never the agent that found the bug. Anthropic, OpenAI and Google each describe a similar validation step before anything reaches a report. The second driver is offense. Anthropic team states that it built its scanner partly because attackers were already using AI models to find exploitable flaws, per The Hacker News. Google opens its Mantis post by noting that models can now discover and exploit bugs with little human help. 1. Claude Security by Anthropic What it is: A multi-agent vulnerability scanner that runs inside a Claude Code session. It is the local version of Anthropic’s hosted Claude Security product, per the plugin README. How it works: Agents map the architecture, build a threat model, hunt across every component and verify each finding independently. The plugin offers 3 jobs from one menu: scan the codebase, scan changes, or suggest patches, per Claude Code docs. Output: A Markdown report along with a SARIF 2.1.0 file for GitHub code scanning. Each finding carries severity, a CWE category, impact and reproduction steps. Patches are drafted in a scratch copy and land as F<n>.patch files. The plugin never commits, pushes or opens a pull request on its own. Cost and access: It makes no model calls of its own, so there is no separate API key. Scans count against your Claude plan’s usage limits. Copy CodeCopiedUse a different Browser/plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official /claude-security Timeline: Anthropic opened a limited preview called Claude Code Security in February 2026. The hosted product reached public beta for Enterprise customers on Claude Opus 4.7. The Claude Code plugin entered beta on July 22, 2026, per Cybersecurity News. In August, the hosted scanner moved to Claude Mythos 5, per Dataconomy. Where it fits: Anthropic positions it as one layer. The security-guidance plugin checks code as Claude writes it, and /security-review does a single pass on a branch. Claude Security is the on-demand deep scan. 2. Codex Security by OpenAI What it is: A CLI and TypeScript SDK, published as @openai/codex-security, for finding, validating and fixing vulnerabilities. How it works: It scans a whole repo, selected paths, or a Git diff. A –mode deep flag runs parallel discovery workers. It validates candidate findings, generates patches and can verify existing fixes. A cs policy command drafts a SECURITY.md that tells future scans what counts as a vulnerability in your project. Output: Threat models, SARIF, JSON or CSV exports, plus publishing to Linear. It can import GitHub code-scanning alerts and suggest owners from Git history. A GitHub Action runs scheduled or pull-request scans; findings are report-only by default. Copy CodeCopiedUse a different Browsernpm install --global @openai/codex-security cs login cs scan Cost and access: The client is Apache-2.0, but the scanner behind it is not. DevOps.com notes the CLI and SDK stay in limited beta for approved customers. The README lists OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, OpenRouter and Fireworks AI as providers. Requires Node.js 22.13+ and Python 3.10+. 3. Security Audit Skill by Cloudflare What it is: An MIT-licensed skill that turns any capable coding agent into a security auditor. How it works: A 6-phase audit: Reconnaissance: map architecture, trust boundaries and input surfaces into architecture.md and a coverage ledger. Coverage-led hunting: isolated hunters each take ledger units; coverage critics look for gaps. Candidate validation: a fresh verifier tries to disprove every unique candidate. Structured output: confirmed, needs_validation and rejected records go to findings.json, checked against a schema. Independent record verification: new agents re-verify every final source claim. Target-neutral reporting: REPORT.md and detail files are derived from the verified records. Requirements: A coding agent that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents, plus Node.js for the validators. It also wants an OS-enforced sandbox with no external network. Without one, leads stay needs_validation instead of being executed. npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill –skill security-audit Then ask the agent: “security audit this codebase.” Output defaults to ~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>, outside your repo. The data behind it: Cloudflare published the skill on June 18, 2026, with its post Build your own vulnerability harness. The roughly 450-line skill seeded an internal harness that now scans 128 repos. Cloudflare reports these lifetime numbers: 20,799 raw candidates from discovery, about 12,057 of which survived validation. 13,841 findings in the shared triage pool across 145 repos, including another harness’s output. 5,442 folded away as duplicates and 1,154 routed out as wrong-repo or low-risk. 7,245 actionable findings sent to engineering teams. Better recon context cut the first-pass rejection rate from 40% to 11%. Cloudflare also uses one model for discovery and a different model for triage, so models check each other. 4. Mantis by Google What it is: An Apache-2.0 set of security-review skills plus an ADK reference harness for AI coding agents. Google team states that it is part of how it finds and fixes bugs internally. How it works: Mantis reads the repo’s history to learn from past security fixes. It builds a hierarchical summary tree, condensing files into directory and root summaries. Google team states that this cut token overhead by over 85%. It then generates a threat model and hypotheses, hunts, deduplicates and critiques findings. What sets it apart: Reproduction and patch verification. Mantis tries to reproduce each bug, from a static exploit sketch up to a unit test or mock server. It patches with an adversarial loop that attacks the fix. It also calibrates severity against a rubric to stop “thousands of criticals.” A mantis-advise skill then feeds what it learned back into code generation. Setup: Clone the repo and point any coding agent at it, or run the ADK harness directly. The harness supports a –focus prompt such as “look for IDOR” and a –max-tokens spend ceiling. articles.title: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.38009v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical chart abstraction transforms unstructured clinical narratives into structured variables for research and quality monitoring. We evaluated a prompting-based large language model (LLM) framework for extracting eight clinical variables from 2,416 neurointerventional acute stroke intervention reports across three hospitals. Twenty-two instruction-tuned open-source LLMs were evaluated across architectures, model sizes, and biomedical adaptations using Quick Response and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting. Non-expert staff annotations served as the cross-model reference standard. Evaluation was restricted to report-variable pairs with a valid LLaMA3.3-70B CoT prediction and a corresponding reference label. Performance measures included extraction accuracy, inference latency, and agreement with expert adjudication. Twenty discordant cases per variable underwent review by two senior physicians and four medical students. LLaMA3.3-70B achieved the highest overall accuracy (94.8%). CoT improved performance on inference-dependent variables such as site of occlusion, while Quick Response was optimal for directly stated procedural fields. Expert adjudication showed that AI predictions were more closely aligned with expert interpretations than non-expert annotations for most variables, with intracranial angioplasty remaining a challenge. Locally deployed LLMs can support scalable clinical information extraction and retrospective stroke registry curation, with expert oversight for ambiguous cases.
articles.summary: 연구진은 3개 병원의 급성 뇌졸중 신경중재 보고서 2,416건에서 임상 변수 8개를 추출하도록 공개 지시 조정 언어 모델 22개를 평가했다. LLaMA3.3-70B가 전체 정확도 94.8%로 가장 높았으며, 추론이 필요한 변수는 사고 과정 유도 방식이, 명시적으로 기재된 항목은 직접 응답 방식이 더 효과적이었다. 다만 모델 간 비교의 기준은 비전문가 주석이었고, 유효한 LLaMA3.3-70B 추론 응답과 참조 라벨이 있는 쌍만 평가에 포함됐다. 일부 불일치 사례의 전문가 재검토는 AI 추출의 유용성을 뒷받침했지만, 모호한 사례에는 감독이 필요하며 실제 임상 배치 성능으로 곧바로 일반화할 수 없다.

articles.title: DeFT-RAG: Incrementally Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.37826v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) lets a large language model (LLM) answer questions by retrieving relevant passages from a large corpus. However, RAG struggles with multi-hop questions, which require chaining facts spread across several documents through intermediate entities that the question never mentions. Graph-based RAG methods retrieve once from the entities a question names and so rarely recover the full evidence chain. Iterative RAG methods recover it step by step, but their accuracy is limited by the many tasks they ask the LLM to perform, such as planning the sub-questions, deciding their dependencies, rewriting them as answers arrive, and keeping track of what is known. We propose DeFT-RAG, a RAG framework built on three components. First, DeFT-RAG generates one self-contained sub-question at a time from the original question and the sub-questions answered so far with their answers (QA pairs). Each sub-question names every entity it asks about, which removes the need to plan, track dependencies or rewrite, and lets the LLM focus on a single fine-grained task at a time. Second, DeFT-RAG moves the remaining LLM work outside the LLM: rule-based updates to a QA table that keeps track of what is known, and yes/no decisions made by a fine-tuned lightweight decision model. Third, DeFT-RAG caches the QA pairs and reuses an answer when a later question asks a sub-question with the same meaning. On MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA and HotpotQA, DeFT-RAG achieves the best accuracy among thirteen baselines with both gpt-4o-mini and Qwen3.6 as the backbone, while giving the LLM fewer input tokens than any other iterative method. With a QA cache shared across 1,000 MuSiQue questions, 23.1% of sub-questions are answered from the cache, which reduces LLM calls by 12.9% without lowering accuracy.
articles.summary: DeFT-RAG는 여러 문서를 연결해야 하는 질문을 독립적으로 이해할 수 있는 하위 질문으로 하나씩 분해하고, 답변을 표와 캐시에 저장하는 검색 증강 생성 프레임워크다. 상태 갱신은 규칙으로 처리하고 단순 판단은 미세조정한 경량 모델에 맡겨, 주 언어 모델이 복잡한 계획과 의존성 관리까지 동시에 수행하는 부담을 줄인다. 연구진은 3개 다중 홉 벤치마크에서 두 백본 모두 13개 비교 방법 중 최고 정확도를 보고했으며, 반복 검색 방식 중 입력 토큰도 가장 적었다고 밝혔다. MuSiQue 1,000개 질문에서 하위 질문의 23.1%를 캐시로 처리해 정확도 저하 없이 모델 호출을 12.9% 줄였다는 결과는 반복적인 기업 지식 질의의 비용 절감 가능성을 보여준다.

articles.title: Artifact Distillation: Training-Free Transfer from Frontier to Small Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.37680v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Closing the gap between frontier and smaller language models is usually approached by distillation: fine-tuning the small model (student) on a frontier model's (teacher) outputs, which binds transfer to training compute and leaves the transferred knowledge largely opaque. We propose Artifact Distillation: a teacher solves training instances and externalizes its problem-solving procedure into an artifact bank that a student queries at inference time, with no gradient updates. Across four LiveBench tasks, a bank written by Claude Opus 4.5 lets Claude Haiku 4.5 outperform unaided Claude Sonnet 4.5 on spatial reasoning (0.707 vs. 0.647) at 60% of its cost, and reach Sonnet 4.5's level on table joining at 89% of its cost. The same raw bank raises Qwen3.5-27B's pooled score from 0.730 to 0.800, showing that transfer is not confined to the teacher's model family.
articles.summary: Artifact Distillation은 강력한 교사 모델이 문제 해결 절차를 외부 자료 저장소로 정리하고, 작은 학생 모델이 추론 시 이를 조회하도록 하는 학습 없는 지식 이전 방식이다. LiveBench 4개 과제 실험에서 Claude Opus 4.5가 만든 자료를 사용한 Haiku 4.5는 공간 추론 점수 0.707로 자료 없이 실행한 Sonnet 4.5의 0.647을 넘었으며 비용은 60% 수준이었다. 같은 자료를 Qwen3.5-27B에 적용해 통합 점수가 0.730에서 0.800으로 상승해 모델 계열 간 이전 가능성도 제시했다. 가중치 갱신 없이 소형 모델을 보강하는 실용적인 접근이지만, 결과는 평가한 과제와 자료 저장소에 한정된다.

articles.title: A Unified Hessian-Guided Framework for Post-Training Quantization
articles.content: Low-bit quantization enables efficient deployment of large language models by reducing memory footprint and computational cost. Achieving high accuracy at low precision requires selecting quantization ranges, linear transformations, and weight rounding decisions. Existing approaches typically optimize these components independently using local reconstruction objectives, which fail to account for the varying impact of quantization errors on downstream predictions. Direct optimization of task-level metrics would provide a more faithful objective, but is challenging due to the discontinuous nature of quantization operations and the high computational cost of evaluating their downstream effects. In this work, we derive a Hessian-guided approximation of the output change induced by joint weight and activation quantization. Based on a tractable Fisher approximation, we formulate a unified post-training quantization framework that enables the joint optimization of quantization ranges, linear transformations, and weight rounding under a common output-sensitivity objective. The resulting method remains practical for modern large language models and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art transformation and rounding methods across both channel-wise and block-wise quantization settings.
articles.summary: 이 연구는 양자화 범위, 선형 변환, 가중치 반올림을 하나의 출력 민감도 목적함수로 함께 최적화하는 학습 후 양자화 프레임워크를 제안했다. 헤시안 기반 출력 변화 근사와 계산 가능한 피셔 근사를 이용해, 개별 계층의 복원 오차만 줄이는 방식보다 최종 예측에 중요한 오류를 반영하도록 설계했다. 채널별·블록별 양자화 모두에서 기존 최상위 변환 및 반올림 방법을 지속적으로 앞섰다고 보고했다. 저비트 언어 모델의 품질 유지에 유용할 수 있으나, 제공된 자료에는 구체적인 비트 수별 성능이나 실제 추론 속도 개선치가 없다.

articles.title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.37732v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many uses of language models end in a typed decision: a choice among a closed set of options, whose probabilities code can act on. Reading those probabilities from one forward pass is fast but often wrong on decisions that take several steps, such as arithmetic, counting, and date comparison. Letting the model think first fixes most of these errors, but costs seconds per decision instead of milliseconds. To pay for thinking only where it helps, ThinkJev builds a fast and a slow system from one open hybrid-thinking model that can answer directly or after a thought. System 1 reads the model's probabilities for the option letters when it answers directly; System 2 reads the same letters after the model has thought on the same cached prompt, so escalating repeats no work and both systems give probabilities over the same options. Because the letters can be read after any number of thought tokens, one sampled thought also gives the answer under every thinking budget. Without training, ThinkJev lets System 1 answer alone only where a statistical test on labeled dev data guarantees that its accepted answers stay under a target error rate. At a 5% target, Qwen3.5-27B answers 24.5% of 8359 test decisions this way with a realized error of 3.9% (Qwen3.5-4B and 9B: 6.5% and 0.0%). For the rest, stopping each thought as soon as its answer is confident reaches 81.6% accuracy, against 82.7% for always thinking, with 72% of the thought tokens. Choosing when to think from System 1's confidence alone saves less, because the decisions System 1 is least sure of are often not the ones thinking fixes. On the public items of JevBench, an independent benchmark of typed-decision services, Qwen3.5-27B thinks on 29.4% and is not distinguishable in accuracy from the two thinking APIs listed (exploratory). Code and data generators are available at https://github.com/ding-xiaolu/ThinkJev.
articles.summary: ThinkJev는 하나의 하이브리드 추론 모델에서 즉시 응답과 사고 후 응답을 결합해, 정해진 선택지의 확률을 반환하는 의사결정 비용을 줄인다. 개발 데이터의 통계 검정으로 빠른 응답을 허용할 범위를 정하고, 나머지는 동일한 캐시 프롬프트에서 추론하다 충분히 확신하면 중단한다. Qwen3.5-27B는 목표 오류율 5% 설정에서 시험 결정의 24.5%를 즉시 처리해 실제 오류율 3.9%를 기록했으며, 나머지의 조기 중단 방식은 항상 추론하는 방식 대비 사고 토큰 72%로 정확도 81.6%를 달성했다. 항상 추론할 때의 82.7%와 비교해 작은 정확도 손실과 비용 절감의 절충을 보여주며, 코드와 데이터 생성기도 공개했다.

articles.title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.37739v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown increasing promise in research-level problem solving, yet a comprehensive collection of such problems is still missing, and evaluating them on research-level problems remains challenging. We introduce OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary resource that combines a structured corpus of open research problems with a retrospective benchmark of recently resolved problems in mathematics. The corpus records problem statements, context, progress, and other information for 12,151 problems. The benchmark contains 200 problems, 110 resolved in 2026 and 90 still open, each with a Lean~4 statement checked by automated probes and two independent reviews; a subset HQ-50 further filters based on quality score, etc. Our evaluation protocol grades formal proofs with two independent checkers in an isolated sandbox under closed-book, frozen-retrieval, and live-web conditions. Evaluating seven LLM agents on the HQ-50 subset under a standardized budget, we find that closed-book rediscovery is rare, at most 7 of 40 resolved problems, whereas live-web success mostly reflects retrieval of published solutions. By linking a broad research-problem corpus to a formally graded evaluation subset with documented solutions, OpenFrontiers provides a foundation for measuring research-level rediscovery and studying progress toward solving currently open scientific problems. The dataset and benchmark could be found in https://huggingface.co/collections/FlippyDora/openfrontiers.
articles.summary: OpenFrontiers는 학문 분야를 아우르는 미해결 연구 문제 12,151개와 수학 문제 200개의 형식 검증 벤치마크를 결합한 자원이다. 벤치마크는 2026년에 해결된 110개 문제와 아직 열린 90개 문제를 포함하며, Lean 4 명제와 독립 검토·증명 검사로 평가 기반을 마련했다. 품질 선별 하위 집합에서 에이전트 7개를 평가한 결과, 외부 자료 없이 해결된 문제를 재발견한 사례는 40개 중 최대 7개였고 실시간 웹 사용의 성공은 주로 공개된 해답 검색을 반영했다. AI의 독창적 연구 능력과 검색 능력을 구분해 측정하는 데 의미가 있으며 데이터셋과 벤치마크를 공개했다.

articles.title: 문어처럼 색 바꾸는 AI 위장 기술, 사람 눈·AI 탐지기 동시 교란…칭화대, 0.4초 환경 적응 구현
articles.content:
중국 칭화대학교(Tsinghua University) 연구진이 문어와 오징어의 위장 능력을 모방해 사람의 눈과 인공지능(AI) 객체 탐지 시스템의 인식을 동시에 어렵게 만드는 동적 위장 기술을 개발했다. 주변 환경을 카메라로 분석하고 AI가 위장 패턴을 생성한 뒤 물체 표면의 디스플레이에 표시하는 방식으로, 환경 변화에 약 0.4초 만에 대응하는 고속 위장 기능을 구현했다.

이번 연구는 기존의 고정된 위장 무늬와 달리 주변 배경에 따라 시각적 특성을 바꿀 수 있다는 점에서 주목된다. 특히 사람에게 자연스럽게 보이는 위장 효과와 AI 객체 탐지 모델의 인식 성능을 낮추는 효과를 함께 고려했다는 것이 핵심이다.

칭화대학교 컴퓨터과학기술학과 후샤오린(Xiaolin Hu) 교수와 주쥔(Jun Zhu) 교수 공동 연구팀은 이러한 기능을 갖춘 생체모방 동적 위장 시스템 '세프캠(CephCam)'을 개발했다. 연구에는 칭화대 심리학과와 베이징대학교(Peking University) 생명과학대학 연구진도 참여했다.

연구 결과는 지난 26일 국제학술지 '네이처 커뮤니케이션스(Nature Communications)'에 '생물학적 시각과 인공 시각의 동시 회피를 위한 두족류 모방 체화형 위장 시스템(Cephalopod-inspired embodied camouflage system for simultaneous evasion of artificial and human visual perception-다운)'이라는 제목으로 발표됐다.

기존 AI 대항 위장 기술은 차량이나 물체 표면에 특수한 무늬를 적용해 객체 탐지 모델의 인식률을 낮추는 방식이 주를 이뤘다. 그러나 AI 탐지를 방해하는 패턴이 사람의 눈에는 오히려 부자연스럽게 보이거나, 특정 환경에서 효과적인 위장이 다른 배경에서는 제대로 작동하지 않는 문제가 있었다.

연구진은 이를 해결하기 위해 문어와 오징어 등 두족류 동물의 '눈·뇌·피부' 구조를 공학적으로 구현했다. 두족류가 주변 환경을 감지하고 피부의 색상과 무늬를 바꾸는 것처럼, 세프캠도 환경 인식부터 위장 패턴 생성, 실제 표면 표시까지 하나의 순환 구조로 연결했다.

시스템의 '눈'에 해당하는 카메라는 주변 배경의 색상과 시각적 특징을 수집한다. 이어 '뇌' 역할을 하는 AI 알고리즘이 환경에 어울리는 위장 패턴을 생성하면서 객체 탐지 모델의 인식 신뢰도를 낮추도록 최적화한다. 마지막으로 '피부'에 해당하는 유기발광다이오드(OLED) 디스플레이가 생성된 패턴을 물체 표면에 표시한다.

특히 연구진은 실제 디스플레이에서 발생하는 색상 차이를 줄이기 위해 컬러넷(ColorNet)이라는 동적 색상 보정 네트워크를 적용했다. 관찰 각도와 조명 조건에 따라 달라지는 색상 표현을 보정해 디지털 환경에서 설계한 위장 패턴이 실제 물리적 환경에서도 최대한 유사하게 나타나도록 했다.

세프캠의 핵심 성과 중 하나는 환경 변화에 대응하는 속도다. 연구진은 위장 패턴을 생성하는 방식을 고속 템플릿 매칭과 정밀 최적화로 구분했다. 고속 모드는 미리 준비된 위장 패턴 가운데 현재 환경과 가장 잘 맞는 것을 선택하는 방식이다. 차량에 장착된 로컬 프로세서에서 작동하며, 새로운 환경에 약 0.4초 만에 적응할 수 있었다.

반면 정밀 모드는 환경인지 위장 생성 알고리즘을 활용해 패턴을 새롭게 최적화한다. 클라우드 연산 환경에서 약 2.5분의 최적화 과정을 거쳐 고속 모드보다 자연스러운 위장 효과와 높은 AI 탐지 회피 성능을 확보했다.

연구진은 두 방식을 결합해 빠른 환경 대응과 정밀한 위장 성능을 함께 확보할 수 있도록 설계했다. 0.4초는 기존 패턴을 선택하는 고속 모드의 처리 시간이며, 새로운 위장 패턴을 처음부터 최적화하는 데 걸리는 시간과는 구분된다.

실험에서는 사람의 시각과 AI 객체 탐지 모델을 대상으로 위장 성능을 각각 검증했다. 연구팀은 112명의 참가자를 대상으로 차량을 찾아내는 시각 탐지 실험을 진행했다. 다양한 환경에서 위장된 차량 이미지를 제시하고 탐지 성공률과 반응 시간을 측정했다.

그 결과 세프캠을 적용한 차량은 기존 비교 방식보다 사람의 탐지 성공률이 낮아졌으며, 차량을 발견한 경우에도 반응 시간이 길어지는 효과가 확인됐다. 이는 사람의 시각적 탐색 과정에서도 위장 효과가 나타났음을 의미한다.

AI 객체 탐지 성능을 평가하는 실험에서도 효과가 확인됐다. 연구진은 여러 딥러닝 기반 객체 탐지 모델을 대상으로 세프캠의 위장 패턴을 적용한 결과, 기존 방식보다 탐지 회피 성능이 향상됐다고 밝혔다.

특히 특정 AI 모델에만 효과적인 위장 패턴을 만드는 데 그치지 않고, 학습 과정에서 사용하지 않은 다른 객체 탐지 모델에도 효과가 나타나도록 여러 모델의 예측 결과를 함께 활용하는 최적화 전략을 적용했다.

물리적 환경에서의 검증도 진행했다. 연구진은 실제 차량 크기의 12분의 1로 제작한 모형에 OLED 디스플레이를 장착하고, 도시·사막·숲·야간·설원 등의 배경 이미지를 인쇄한 실험 환경에서 위장 성능을 측정했다.

카메라로 촬영한 실제 모형의 영상을 AI 객체 탐지 모델에 입력해 관찰 거리와 각도에 따른 인식 결과를 비교했다. 이를 통해 디지털 시뮬레이션에서 설계한 위장 패턴이 실제 디스플레이를 장착한 물체에서도 작동할 수 있음을 확인했다.

이번 연구는 인간과 AI의 시각 인식 방식이 서로 다르더라도, 두 시스템의 탐지 성능을 동시에 낮출 수 있는 시각적 조건이 존재한다는 점을 보여준다.

일반적으로 딥러닝 기반 객체 탐지 모델은 이미지의 질감과 국소적인 특징에 민감하게 반응하는 반면, 사람은 물체의 형태와 주변 맥락을 함께 고려하는 경향이 있다. 세프캠은 이러한 차이를 고려하면서도 주변 배경과 자연스럽게 어울리는 패턴을 생성하도록 설계됐다.

연구진은 이번 기술이 시각적 개인정보 보호와 AI 감시 기술의 안전성 평가, 실제 환경에 적응하는 생체모방 시스템 연구 등에 활용될 가능성이 있다고 설명했다.

동시에 AI 기반 감시와 객체 인식 시스템의 취약성을 보여준다는 점에서 기술의 오용 가능성과 탐지 시스템의 신뢰성 문제도 함께 제기된다. 다만 이번 연구는 디지털 시뮬레이션과 축소 차량 모형을 중심으로 진행됐다. 실제 크기의 차량이나 복잡한 도로 환경에서 동일한 성능이 구현됐는지는 검증되지 않았으며, 모든 AI 감시 카메라와 객체 탐지 시스템을 회피할 수 있다는 의미도 아니다.

특히 정밀 위장 패턴 생성에는 클라우드 서버의 연산 자원이 필요하다는 점에서 처리 지연과 통신 의존성도 해결해야 할 과제로 남아 있다.

이번 연구는 AI가 물리적 환경을 인식하고 판단한 결과를 실제 하드웨어의 동작으로 연결하는 피지컬 AI(Physical AI)와 체화형 인공지능(Embodied AI) 연구의 한 사례로도 볼 수 있다. 주변 환경을 감지하고, AI가 대응 방식을 결정한 뒤, 물체 표면을 변화시키고 다시 환경을 분석하는 폐쇄루프 구조를 구현했다는 점에서다.

향후 이러한 기술은 변화하는 환경에 스스로 적응하는 지능형 소재와 로봇 시스템 연구로 확장될 가능성이 있다. 동시에 AI 시각 인식 기술이 실제 물리적 환경에서 얼마나 안정적으로 작동하는지 평가하는 새로운 연구 과제도 제시하고 있다.
articles.summary: 칭화대 등 연구진이 카메라, AI 패턴 생성, OLED 표면 표시를 연결해 사람과 AI 객체 탐지기의 인식을 동시에 어렵게 하는 동적 위장 시스템 CephCam을 개발했다는 보도다. ColorNet 색상 보정 네트워크로 관찰 각도와 조명에 따른 실제 디스플레이 색상 차이를 보완한다. 약 0.4초라는 적응 시간은 미리 준비한 패턴을 고르는 로컬 고속 모드의 수치이며, 새 패턴을 정밀 최적화하는 클라우드 모드는 약 2.5분이 걸린다. 물리적 환경에서 비전 모델의 취약성을 검토하는 데 의미가 있지만, 제공된 내용에는 인간 대상 실험의 최종 효과 수치가 없어 회피 성능을 정량적으로 판단하기 어렵다.

articles.title: Exposure Is Not Commitment: Double-Stratified Evaluation of Latent Monitors for Tool-Using Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.37679v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tool-using language agents are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection, and a growing literature probes model internals to catch unsafe actions before they execute, with sharply conflicting results. We argue much of the conflict is an evaluation artifact, and propose a double-stratification protocol: separate injection exposure from behavioral commitment, in both the evaluation and the training population. On the primary Qwen AgentDojo grid, monitors trained on the naive mixed unsafe-versus-rest contrast mostly learn exposure: they flag exposed trajectories whether or not the agent complies, and barely predict which cases turn unsafe. Retrained on exposed cases only, the same probe families predict the model's own unsafe tool call up to two steps early, the maximum the three-step trajectories admit (logistic AUROC 0.853, matched by a trained TF-IDF text baseline at 0.855). Mistral-7B reaches 0.896 and OLMo-2-7B 0.912; their naive contrasts learn different things: inverted exposure ranking on one, both axes on the other. Representations separate on exposure (probe 1.000 versus trained text 0.908) and where visible context is sanitized or unavailable. Training contrast alone reproduces the shape of recent pre-action-probe negative results, one candidate explanation for the conflict: the signal exists, but the model's own zero-shot forecast and NLA verbalizations do not reliably recover it. An unstratified AUROC overstates what a latent monitor knows, and what a naive contrast learns is population-dependent: evaluations should stratify both.
articles.summary: 이 연구는 도구 사용 에이전트의 내부 상태 감시기가 프롬프트 주입에 노출된 사실과 실제로 위험한 행동을 하려는 상태를 구분해야 한다고 주장한다. Qwen AgentDojo 실험에서 단순한 위험·비위험 혼합 학습은 주로 노출 여부를 학습했지만, 노출 사례 안에서 다시 학습하면 위험한 도구 호출을 최대 두 단계 전에 AUROC 0.853으로 예측했다. 다만 같은 조건의 학습된 TF-IDF 텍스트 기준선도 0.855를 기록해 내부 표현의 우위가 보편적으로 입증된 것은 아니다. 에이전트 안전 감시를 도입할 때 노출과 행동을 나눠 평가하지 않으면 탐지 능력을 과대평가할 수 있다는 실무적 경고다.

articles.title: SkillMem: Compact External Skill Memory for Latent Multi-Agent Reasoning
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.37935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Latent multi-agent systems reduce inference cost by keeping intermediate reasoning and inter-agent communication in continuous representations.\ Reusable skills, however, are commonly supplied as text or stored as layer-wise Key-Value states or skill-specific model parameters, introducing repeated processing or substantial per-skill storage.\ We introduce \textbf{SkillMem}, which represents each reusable skill as a small external latent memory and makes it directly available during latent multi-agent reasoning.\ A role-conditioned cross-attention reader allows the same memory to guide different agents according to their roles and current hidden states.\ We train the skill memories and shared reader through behavioral distillation, matching the change in token predictions induced by a textual skill while keeping the backbone frozen.\ For our experiments, we obtain textual skills from paired successful and failed multi-agent trajectories, although existing skills can also be compiled directly.\ Across six benchmarks and Qwen3 models ranging from 4B to 14B parameters, SkillMem provides strong gains for smaller backbones while preserving efficient latent multi-agent inference across model scales.\ We use the same $8\times256$ memory configuration across all evaluated model scales, requiring 9.6\,KB of skill-specific storage per skill, including its retrieval embedding.\ For a library of 100 skills, SkillMem reduces total storage by more than $38\times$ compared with alternative skill representations and achieves up to a $4.23\times$ end-to-end inference speedup.\ These results show that compact procedural memories can be reused without sacrificing the efficiency of latent multi-agent reasoning.
articles.summary: SkillMem은 잠재 표현으로 소통하는 다중 에이전트가 재사용할 기술을 작은 외부 잠재 메모리로 저장하고, 역할 조건부 교차 어텐션으로 읽게 하는 방법이다. 백본 모델을 동결한 채 텍스트 기술이 유도하는 토큰 예측 변화를 행동 증류로 학습해, 반복적인 텍스트 처리와 대용량 기술별 저장을 줄인다. Qwen3 4B~14B와 6개 벤치마크에서 기술당 9.6KB 구성을 사용했고, 기술 100개 라이브러리는 대안 대비 저장 공간을 38배 넘게 줄이며 최대 4.23배의 종단 간 추론 속도 향상을 보였다고 보고했다. 특히 작은 백본의 성능 개선이 두드러져, 경량 다중 에이전트의 절차 지식 재사용에 유망하지만 범용 서비스에서의 효과는 추가 검증이 필요하다.
